source_record.title: Mixed cash/electronic checkout cannot confirm its electronic leg
source_record.trigger_and_safe_repro_design: On approved disposable DB only: order 200 EGP split 100 cash + 100 InstaPay; checkout succeeds and posts cash; confirm electronic. Expected second leg succeeds; static code deterministically rejects existing sale journal. No such write executed.
source_record.root_cause: Checkout starts/completes sale-{request} for immediate mixed leg; confirmation attempts TryStart identical completed key. Movement suffix does not separate journal.
source_record.correction_design: Journal payment events per stable leg identity, not whole mixed order; electronic confirmation must atomically persist pending-to-confirmed and one deferred leg movement. Preserve idempotent replay; do not remove original journal to workaround.
source_record.regression_tests: Integration mixed cash+InstaPay and card+Wallet confirm/retry/concurrent confirm, exactly correct per-channel sums and one movement per leg; compare replay movement IDs.
source_record.counterevidence_and_limits: Independent printing/workflows review via parent confirmed unsuffixed completed journal collision. Existing domain mixed split tests prove DefersAllMoney false; integration confirmation tests only single InstaPay.
source_record.independent_challenge: Independent printing/workflows review via parent confirmed unsuffixed completed journal collision. Existing domain mixed split tests prove DefersAllMoney false; integration confirmation tests only single InstaPay. Parent also independently confirmed full CheckoutRules-to-checkout-journal-to-confirm chain.

implementation_readiness.impact: Mixed cash/electronic checkout can post the immediate tender but reject confirmation of the deferred electronic leg because both paths claim the same completed sale journal key; electronic collection may remain unconfirmed.
implementation_readiness.proposed_remediation: Journal idempotency per stable payment-leg identity. Atomically transition pending electronic leg to confirmed and post exactly one leg movement; preserve whole-order and replay semantics without deleting an existing journal as a workaround.
regression_tests: Mixed cash+InstaPay and card+Wallet checkout, confirmation, retry, and concurrent confirm; verify exact tender totals and one movement per leg.
Replay same request and verify stable movement identity.
acceptance_criteria: Each tender leg can complete independently and exactly once.
Confirmed electronic state and its movement commit atomically; channel totals reconcile.
counterevidence: Canonical record says mixed split makes DefersAllMoney false; existing confirmation integration covers only single InstaPay.
No runtime reproduction in saved evidence.

source_record.title: Cancelling pending mixed electronic payment hides collected cash without reversal
source_record.trigger_and_safe_repro_design: Disposable DB: 200 EGP split cash 100 + InstaPay 100, cancel pending transfer. Actual 100 cash and sale_collection remain; cash sales query now returns zero because order cancelled. Close with actual cash yields false overage/revenue omission.
source_record.root_cause: Whole-order cancellation assumes checkout deferred all money, false for Multi. No refund/reversal of immediate legs; reports exclude cancelled order.
source_record.correction_design: Model leg cancellation and outstanding tender replacement, or require explicit approved immediate-leg refund before full cancellation. Preserve cash until real reversal, and clearly classify inventory waste policy.
source_record.regression_tests: Cancel split cash/electronic and card/electronic; assert treasury and operational cash totals reconcile, refunded immediate leg only when money returned, concurrent cancel/confirm exactly one terminal outcome.
source_record.counterevidence_and_limits: Multi orders supported by checkout/domain; integration cancel helper creates only single InstaPay so test does not disprove. Inventory no reversal is separately deliberate legacy policy, not main defect.
source_record.independent_challenge: printing_workflows independently traced all listed source paths; counterevidence searched: permission/approval and pooled balance do not prove collected funds, account locks do not refresh invoice outstanding, same-key dedup does not cover different operations. No runtime writes.

implementation_readiness.impact: Cancelling an order with an already-collected immediate split leg can mark whole order cancelled and remove it from sales reporting while leaving collected cash without reversal, making drawer/revenue totals inconsistent.
implementation_readiness.proposed_remediation: Model tender-leg cancellation/outstanding replacement; or require approved refund/reversal for already collected legs before full order cancellation. Keep collected cash represented until a real reversal; state explicit inventory waste policy.
regression_tests: Cancel cash+electronic and card+electronic orders; reconcile treasury, operational cash, and reports.
Race cancel against confirm and require one terminal tender outcome.
Verify refund only when funds are actually returned.
acceptance_criteria: Cancelled order/payment state preserves every collected tender until a matching reversal exists.
Order, tender, treasury, and report totals reconcile after either winning race.
counterevidence: Current integration cancel helper creates only single InstaPay; it does not exercise mixed split.
Inventory non-reversal may be deliberate legacy policy and is outside core cash issue.
unresolved_owner_policy: Confirm intended cancellation/refund semantics for immediate collected legs and inventory waste.

source_record.title: Refund can debit money for an order that was never collected
source_record.trigger_and_safe_repro_design: Disposable DB with funded drawer/InstaPay: create unpaid cash-on-delivery or pending single InstaPay order, request legitimate approved refund. Total remaining >0 and pooled balance sufficient; path posts refund despite no collection. Wallet unprotected balance makes negative account possible as existing policy.
source_record.root_cause: Refund eligibility based payable Total minus prior refunds, rather than collected refundable amount; domain never asserts IsPaid or confirmed/settled collection.
source_record.correction_design: Compute per-order settled less already refunded, require collection provenance; pending orders cancel through proper path. Revalidate under same order lock. Domain invariant should reject unpaid full-order refund too.
source_record.regression_tests: Unpaid COD, pending InstaPay/Wallet, partial collected mixed unsupported, full/partial paid, cancellation/refund/confirm races; assert uncollected requests write no movements/refunds and leave balances unchanged.
source_record.counterevidence_and_limits: Approval authorizes action but cannot prove money collected. Protected-source pooled balance only covers liquidity. Multi already rejected; unaffected paid single methods work.
source_record.independent_challenge: printing_workflows independently traced all listed source paths; counterevidence searched: permission/approval and pooled balance do not prove collected funds, account locks do not refresh invoice outstanding, same-key dedup does not cover different operations. No runtime writes.

implementation_readiness.impact: Refund handler can use order total less prior refunds rather than settled collection provenance, allowing an authorized refund against an unpaid/pending order if source path permits; pooled account balance only ensures liquidity, not collection.
implementation_readiness.proposed_remediation: Derive refundable limit from settled tender legs less prior refunds; require source collection proof. Route pending orders through cancellation. Revalidate under the same order lock and reject unpaid refunds in the domain invariant.
regression_tests: Unpaid COD, pending electronic, confirmed paid, partial collected, and unsupported mixed cases.
Race refund with cancel/confirm and concurrent refunds; rejected cases create no refund/movement and balances remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Cumulative refunds never exceed the order’s actually settled amount per tender leg.
Rejected unpaid refund leaves no partial writes; valid refund atomically records refund and outflow.
counterevidence: Approval permission does not prove collection. Pooled protected balance checks cash availability only. Multi case already rejected; paid single-method refund remains supported.

source_record.title: Historical cash refund omitted from current-shift expected cash
source_record.trigger_and_safe_repro_design: Sell cash in shift A then close A; open B with 500 EGP float; refund A order 100 from B. Refund movement operational B but orders for B exclude A and movement selection excludes refund; expected remains 500 while actual 400. Original shift historical query also changes from new RefundAmount.
source_record.root_cause: Drawer mixes lifetime order net amounts with selected operational movement types and does not allocate refunds by OperationalShiftId.
source_record.correction_design: Compute drawer receipts/disbursements from posted operational drawer movements or explicitly join OrderRefund operational shift; prevent double deduction for same-shift refunds and preserve old closed snapshot. Distinguish original sales day from refund execution day.
source_record.regression_tests: Historical A -> B cash refund actual/expected and final drawer zero after close; same-shift partial refund once; noncash historic; cross-business-day report reconciliation; repeat request idempotent.
source_record.counterevidence_and_limits: Refund rules explicitly promise historical immutability, and current shift required. Existing domain test checks chosen operational shift only; no reconciliation composition in inspected tests.
source_record.independent_challenge: printing_workflows independently traced all listed source paths; counterevidence searched: permission/approval and pooled balance do not prove collected funds, account locks do not refresh invoice outstanding, same-key dedup does not cover different operations. No runtime writes.

implementation_readiness.impact: A cash refund executed during current shift B for a sale from shift A may reduce lifetime/order net while the drawer reconciliation for B omits the refund outflow or allocates it to the original sale; expected cash and actual drawer diverge.
implementation_readiness.proposed_remediation: Compute drawer flow from posted operational cash movements or join refund rows by OperationalShiftId; avoid double deduction for same-shift refunds and preserve immutable closed shift snapshots. Separate original sale period from refund execution period.
regression_tests: Historical shift A sale refunded in B; verify B actual/expected and final close balance reconcile.
Same-shift partial cash refund counted exactly once.
Historic noncash refund and cross-business-day reports preserve attribution; idempotent retry.
acceptance_criteria: Each refund cash outflow appears once in the shift/business period in which it was executed.
Historical closed shift snapshot remains immutable; current operational drawer reconciles to movements.
counterevidence: Refund rules explicitly promise historical immutability and current shift is required. Existing domain test checks operational shift selection but not reconciliation composition.
unresolved_owner_policy: Confirm report presentation of original sale period versus refund execution period if business reports aggregate them differently.

source_record.title: Concurrent distinct invoice settlements can overpay supplier and corrupt invoice cache
source_record.trigger_and_safe_repro_design: Disposable DB invoice outstanding 100 EGP, source account 1000. Two requests different RequestIds both pre-read 100, each pays 80. Account lock serializes account only; second never refreshes invoice. Ledger receives total160 while invoice stale Paid80/Remaining20.
source_record.root_cause: Business invariant checked outside transaction and unrelated account lock; purchase has no concurrency token or invoice row lock.
source_record.correction_design: Acquire invoice UPDLOCK/HOLDLOCK in transaction before reading outstanding and tracked state; requery supplier invoice ledger under protection, validate then post/cache. Stable lock ordering relative to account and approvals; unique keys remain for replay.
source_record.regression_tests: Barrier-controlled two distinct 80 payments against 100 from same and different accounts: one succeeds, one rejects, total <=100, caches equal ledger; same-request retry replays.
source_record.counterevidence_and_limits: Treasury lock protects account from negative pooled balance but cannot make stale outstanding fresh. Different IDs legitimately bypass idempotency. No runtime reproduction performed.
source_record.independent_challenge: printing_workflows independently traced all listed source paths; counterevidence searched: permission/approval and pooled balance do not prove collected funds, account locks do not refresh invoice outstanding, same-key dedup does not cover different operations. No runtime writes.

citation_correction.reason: Legacy DbContext309-328 was real Customer/Delivery source, irrelevant to Purchase concurrency. Correct Purchase/Payment/SupplierLedger mappings277-305 and actual fields now cited.
citation_correction.disposition: Finding survives qualified static challenge; no new count or runtime reproduction.

citation_correction_history.reason: Actual source has111 lines; final payment/ledger range75-112 corrected to75-111. No reasoning or finding count change.

implementation_readiness.impact: Two distinct authorized settlements can each read the same invoice outstanding and overpay supplier; invoice cache may then diverge from ledger. Source-account locking can preserve cash solvency while invoice obligation is exceeded.
implementation_readiness.proposed_remediation: Within one transaction lock the invoice row before loading outstanding and tracked balance, recompute from supplier-invoice ledger under that lock, validate and atomically post settlement/cache. Define stable invoice/account/approval lock order; retain request idempotency.
regression_tests: Barrier: two different 80 settlements against outstanding 100, both same account and different accounts; at most one succeeds, total <=100 and cache equals ledger.
Same request replay returns committed result.
acceptance_criteria: For each invoice, committed settlements never exceed current outstanding.
Cached paid/outstanding fields match ledger under serialized settlements.
Retries remain idempotent and deadlock policy is bounded.
counterevidence: Treasury lock protects pooled source balance but not invoice freshness. Distinct request IDs legitimately bypass same-key idempotency. No race was executed.

source_record.trigger_and_safe_repro_design: Two authorized backups of same database/directory choose timestamps within same UTC second; paths identical. Later BACKUP ... FORMAT can replace earlier backup media. Records now share file; retention of one may delete another supposedly preserved file. Never execute this against user backup files; deterministic path function test sufficient.
source_record.root_cause: Second-resolution timestamp treated as unique filename; no GUID/exclusive reservation. Retention reasons over records not unique physical paths.
source_record.correction_design: Use collision-resistant unique ID in filename and prohibit overwriting existing destination; preserve record-to-file identity. Retention should validate canonical distinct paths and never delete a file referenced by retained record.
source_record.regression_tests: Same-time parallel name generation unique; simulated same destination refused; pruning duplicate path references preserves retained valid backup. Isolated SQL integration later with explicit permission.
source_record.counterevidence_and_limits: SQL concurrency might make one backup fail instead of overwrite; either violates no-collision claim. Exact physical media behavior not runtime tested. Scheduled/interactive callers can overlap.

independent_challenge.reasoning: Filename contains only database and UTC timestamp to seconds; two authorized same-directory requests in same second choose same path, regardless distinct row GUID. BACKUP WITH FORMAT permits media replacement. Simultaneous SQL calls can instead fail; no particular concurrency outcome asserted. Sequential short backups can collide too. Retention protects newest valid record ID but does not deduplicate underlying paths, so duplicate records undermine file identity protection.
independent_challenge.counterevidence: Destination requires authorized backup actor/configured directory, SQL permissions and actual engine file access. COPY_ONLY preserves external backup-chain semantics; values parameterized and database identifier validated. No anonymous SQL injection claim.

Checkout stages Pending and Complete in same scoped transaction before save/commit; another context cannot treat that as reliable census of running requests. After safety backup returns119 and before SINGLE_USER153, new financial request may commit and acknowledge. Restore replaces it, while earlier safety backup need not contain it. Later SQL exclusive access occurs too late to close this gap.

Planned rollback of post-backup history is inherent; finding concerns acknowledged work accepted during purported safe maintenance window. source_record.title: First stock receipt can race unit-change admission and reinterpret movement history

source_evidence.trigger: Initially valid inventory item with UnitA and no stock movements. Authorized inventory_manage update requests distinct UnitB. Separately authorized purchasing receipt for same existing item uses positive quantity/cost, credit payment0, valid supplier/open day, fresh IDs.
schedule: UpdateInventory loads item81 and checks unitChanged84, then StockMovements.Any87 returnsfalse and Domain guard88 accepts; pause before Save100.

ReceivePurchase commits a legitimate PurchaseReceipt In movement with quantity milliunits in previously current UnitA: stock167-175, Save207/Commit208. Choose complete receipt before metadata writer resumes, so transactions need not overlap.

source_evidence.root_cause: Immutable-unit predicate is evaluated before write without coordinating the first stock-movement admission. InventoryItem mapping244 is primary key only, no concurrency token; movement FK protects existence, not unit interpretation.

counterevidence: If movement already exists when update query runs, guard correctly rejects; selected first-movement race avoids that ordinary protection.

implementation_readiness.source_confirmed_behavior: BusinessDayRules.CalculateDenominationCount clamps negative quantities to zero, but accepts denomination values and positive quantities without visible range/whitelist validation, multiplying and summing signed long values and subtracting expected cash. SaveCashCountHandler forwards request rows and ExpectedPiastres into this calculation and persists the count and a cash_count_finalized audit event in one SaveChanges call. The request contract allows arbitrary long denomination and quantity values. Endpoint delegates to this handler.
implementation_readiness.root_cause: Arithmetic and domain validation are not bounded at the finalization boundary; persisted audit data records the derived result without enforcing the supported denomination set or representable totals.
implementation_readiness.preconditions: Authenticated/authorized cash_count actor; existing business day; crafted request values beyond the normal denomination list. For misstatement, inputs must reach signed overflow or use unsupported denominations/expected amount. Negative quantity behavior is explicitly a compatibility clamp.
implementation_readiness.impact: Could finalize and audit a mathematically incorrect cash total/difference. Existing evidence does not show direct treasury posting, shift settlement, or close-blocker override; do not characterize as cash loss.
counterevidence: Normal denomination-list endpoint returns fixed valid notes/coins; normal UI path need not generate arbitrary denomination IDs.
Authorization and business-day existence checks gate handler.
Negative quantity clamping is documented intended compatibility behavior and should not be casually removed.
Saved isolated pure reproduction is not actual net8 application/database acceptance; host/build checked-arithmetic overrides were not certified.
implementation_readiness.proposed_fix_or_owner_decision: Owner must first decide whether ExpectedPiastres is a client-supplied comparison target or must be derived from a server-authoritative snapshot. Then whitelist supported positive denominations and bound each quantity/aggregate; use checked multiply, sum, and difference and convert overflow/invalid rows to explicit domain rejection. Preserve agreed negative-quantity compatibility semantics or reject only by explicit policy.
regression_tests: Domain tests for every allowed denomination, unsupported/zero/negative denomination, maximum quantity, multiplication overflow, aggregate overflow, and difference overflow.
Authorized handler test proves invalid input creates neither count nor audit record; valid input persists exact values atomically.
Endpoint test verifies invalid input maps to a deliberate client error.
Verify whether finalized cash-count data participates in close reconciliation and that any such use is server-validated.
Build/run arithmetic behavior under the actual net8 deployment configuration.
acceptance_criteria: All accepted values fall within explicit denomination and monetary bounds; no wraparound reaches persisted count/audit.
Rejected values produce no partial count/audit writes.
ExpectedPiastres authority and negative quantity semantics are documented and covered.
Any reconciliation consumer uses the validated result or independently recomputes the expected value.

source_record.title: Standalone employee settlements remain payable through frozen period payroll
source_record.root_cause: PayrollRules computes payroll from earning categories and named deductions but ignores standalone Settlement debits. PayEmployee reduces current balance, while CreatePayroll freezes period net and PayPayroll pays that frozen amount without revalidating outstanding employee balance.
source_record.source_mechanism: For a current-period earned amount of 20,000 piastres, standalone payout can debit 20,000 and reduce current balance to zero. The period payroll input still contains the earning; Settlement is not subtracted, so the frozen net can remain 20,000. Paying the run can issue another 20,000 treasury outflow and PayrollSettlement. This is source-derived arithmetic only.
source_record.impact: If both payment modes are applied to the same earned obligation, the employee can receive the same earnings twice and the ledger can become negative by the duplicated amount. Real usage and intended treatment are unverified.
preconditions: Same-period earnings are posted and included in payroll lines.
The same obligation is first settled using PayEmployee, before payroll creation or after the run is frozen.
An authorized user can use both employees_ledger and payroll_pay flows, or separate authorized users do so.
The approved payroll run is later paid from a sufficiently funded account.
counterevidence: Source explicitly supports standalone payment without a payroll run and separately supports period payroll; the wording does not establish mutual exclusion.
Settlement and PayrollSettlement are distinct ledger classifications and the two paths have different permissions, but neither distinction itself nets or blocks the same obligation.
Financial continuation reviewer confirms source mechanics, but policy exclusivity, owner policy, live usage, and runtime reproduction are unverified.
Existing tests cover each payment path separately and do not exercise the combined same-period sequence.
FIN-006 (generic Paid transition) and FIN-012 (attendance correction credit excluded) are related payroll risks but distinct causes.
source_record.recommendation: Clarify whether standalone Settlement is a prepayment of the same earnings included in period payroll. If both paths may cover one obligation, make payroll calculate and pay only the remaining liability, including the case where settlement occurs after a run is frozen; otherwise enforce and test exclusive payment modes for each period. Preserve the separate audit classifications.
required_regression_tests: DailyWage then standalone settlement then create and pay the same-period payroll; verify total disbursement does not exceed the earned obligation.
Create/approve a run, then standalone settlement, then pay the frozen run; verify prior settlement cannot be paid again.
Test that unrelated-period settlements do not reduce the wrong payroll period.
Verify idempotent replays of both modes do not create duplicate treasury or employee ledger movements.

independent_verification.disposition: Retain as a source-confirmed cross-flow accounting risk / requirements question pending explicit policy and usage confirmation; do not promote duplicate-pay as a canonical defect from the available evidence.
independent_verification.scope: Independent source challenge agrees overlap mechanics are real and finds no source exclusivity rule, but explicitly does not confirm duplicate-pay defect or severity from available evidence.

source_record.distinctness: Not present as a duplicate-pay finding in canonical registry as of source dedup check; existing FIN-006 and FIN-012 concern different mechanisms.

implementation_readiness.impact: If standalone Settlement is a prepayment of earnings already included in the same frozen payroll, paying both paths can disburse the same obligation twice; source flow shows this mechanism but does not establish the accounting policy or an actual duplicate payout.
implementation_readiness.proposed_remediation: Owner decision first. If settlements prepay same-period earnings, derive remaining liability from an explicit period/earning obligation and apply settlements both before payroll calculation and after run freeze; if the two paths are mutually exclusive, enforce atomic exclusion on both. Preserve frozen-run, replay, audit, source-balance, and historical-record behavior.
regression_tests: Create earnings, settle same obligation standalone, then create/approve/pay payroll; total disbursement must satisfy owner-approved invariant.
Create/approve payroll, apply standalone settlement, then pay frozen payroll; same invariant.
Unrelated-period settlement must not be netted.
Repeat and concurrent requests with distinct IDs; validate exactly-once employee ledger and treasury effects in approved disposable SQL Server integration DB.
acceptance_criteria: Written owner policy defines relationship between standalone Settlement and period payroll obligation.
Tests implement that policy across both sequence orders, period boundaries, retries and concurrent requests.
No duplicate obligation disbursement if policy treats Settlement as prepayment; otherwise distinct obligation is explicitly represented and reported.
counterevidence: Standalone PayEmployee locks employee ledger balance and atomically posts Settlement plus treasury movement.
Code comments describe a separate any-time payment mode, which may imply intentional independence.
Payroll calculation omits Settlement and PayPayroll pays frozen NetPayable, but absence in reviewed paths does not establish system-wide policy or all-path exclusivity.
Coordinator cross-check expressly keeps duplicate payment conditional and reports no combined SQL/runtime sequence.
unresolved_owner_policy: Is standalone employee Settlement a prepayment against earnings included in period payroll, or a distinct payable obligation?
If it is a prepayment, how should settlement after payroll freeze affect already-approved NetPayable: block, adjust/reopen, or record a separate recovery?
implementation_readiness.limitations: Source-confirmed flow and atomicity only; policy, actual sequence, SQL/provider behavior and duplicate-payment realization unverified. Do not promote to confirmed duplicate-payment defect.

source_record.title: Two machines can submit the same pending kitchen job

source_record.repro: In an isolated fake/server harness, let two agents with separate journals and machines request the same route before either reports. Both obtain the same Pending job, both send, then each reports with a different attempt ID. No physical reproduction performed.
source_record.root_cause: No server-side atomic claim, station ownership, lease or fencing token exists. Report idempotency protects reporting replay, not independent physical attempts.
source_record.tests: Existing PrintAgentTests cover route selection and one-agent report retry only; add concurrent two-agent claim/fencing test, and replacement-agent unknown-outcome recovery.
source_record.recommendation: Introduce server-side station/route registration and atomic claimed dispatch with fencing; require explicit operator handling for uncertain physical outcomes. Lease expiry alone cannot guarantee exactly-once paper.
source_record.uncertainty: Duplicate deployment is the trigger; one machine mutex plus one correctly configured agent per route limits exposure. Physical exactly-once remains impossible without printer acknowledgement/operator reconciliation.

source_record.title: PIN-bearing user-management requests are durably stored as unencrypted JSON
evidence_chain: App constructor configures actual cashier file store before view-model field initializers.
Users action DTO carries InitialPin or CurrentPin/NewPin; durable owner keys users.create and users.change-pin are explicit.
RetainedRequest.SendAsync persists first unresolved DTO before transport; ambiguous outcome retains the exact object.
FileRetainedRequestStore.Save serializes Payload=request without exclusion or encryption, writes plain text temp, then moves to station LocalApplicationData JSON.
preconditions: Actual user-management operation with PIN-bearing fields and working durable store.
Access to the Windows profile journal, its filesystem copies/backup, or another permitted local collection mechanism while data remains.
counterevidence: Windows profile ACLs constrain access; no ACL deficiency demonstrated.
First known result, including definite initial rejection, clears the journal; known successful resolution clears recovered records.
Unwritable persistence may leave no file; observed source behavior is not proof every real station has exposed records.
Separate station directories reduce cross-client mixing but are not credential encryption.
source_record.impact: Credential values may survive transient UI entry in local unencrypted recovery state; no unauthenticated remote disclosure, arbitrary login or server PIN hash weakness established.

independent_verification.scope: Local plaintext serialization confirmed; actual deployment exposure and ACL access unverified

source_record.recommendation: Design credential-free durable recovery/status using server-owned request identity; minimize secret retention. If unavoidable, choose approved per-user protected storage and explicit lifecycle, but encryption alone does not replace recovery design. No fix implemented.
required_regression_tests: In-memory fake-store serialization tests asserting all PIN values absent from durable representations.
Create/change PIN known success, known initial failure, ambiguous timeout and recovered success without secret persistence.
User/station identity scoping, migration of preexisting journals only through explicitly authorized safe handling.
regression_risks: Removing recovery fields without protocol change could strand ambiguous account creation/change or cause repeated credential changes.
source_record.remaining_uncertainty: No actual journal, credential, filesystem ACL or deployed backup collected. Independent source challenge and owner retention policy remain pending.
source_record.additional_source_observation: If temporary write succeeds but File.Move fails, exception is swallowed; Clear removes only main JSON. A leftover temp can retain same plaintext. No actual leftover file observed.

qualifications: Same-process retry correctly preserves immutable request and original key in sampled paths.
Normal close/lock gates mitigate accidental exit.
Backend same-key idempotency still works; loss of key does not itself prove duplicate transaction.
CallCenter normal checkout and other RetainedRequest-based operations must not be generalized into this sampled gap.
This review independently covered checkout/expense/refund/treasury only; additional safe-drop/cash-movement/shift paths need their own source evidence.

source_record.title: Primary cashier and treasury money requests lose original retry identity on process loss

evidence.explanation: Exact checkout retained only in private field; no journal save/recover.
Drawer expense private pending field and rotating ID.
Refund request and identity stored only in memory.
Treasury deposit/withdraw/transfer retained as in-memory delegate.
Durable helper exists but these money operations do not use it.
Cashier Operations safe-drop request and pending DTO remain in view-model fields; retries retain key only while that object/process remains alive.
Control Center safe-drop uses stable owner-keyed RetainedRequest and retries/reloads the request; same workflow has stronger but best-effort persistence.
Store catches write/replace errors and invokes optional callback; app bootstraps without callback, while operation proceeds.
Test checks same-instance request replay, not process restart or disk persistence.

source_record.trigger: Server may commit request, response is lost, cashier process is terminated or power is lost before outcome resolved; operator reconstructs same operation after restart.
source_record.rootCause: Normal close/edit gates and same-process fixed keys cannot preserve immutable submitted DTO/key across forced termination. Primary financial partials bypass existing durable helper.
source_record.impact: No reliable station-owned recovery question for original checkout/refund/expense/treasury action; manually repeating with new key can create duplicate real operations. Actual duplicate ledger writes NOT tested.
counterarguments: Server idempotency prevents repeat of SAME request ID, but restarted UI mints a new ID.
Normal close gate is present; it cannot intercept power loss.
CallCenter checkout already persists operator-scoped DTO, so finding does not apply to its normal write path.
regressionTests: Simulate committed-but-lost-response with fake transport, reconstruct actual cashier VM/session with store, assert exact request ID/payload recovered before any new action.
Repeat for refund, expense, safe drop, drawer transfer, shift open/close and treasury operations; assert server ledger unaffected on replay in isolated integration fixture.
source_record.recommendation: Persist exact versioned typed financial request and owner before dispatch; expose recovery by original identity, block replacement until outcome known; no fixes performed.

findings.title: Distinct concurrent business-day opens can pass pre-insert active-state validation

independent_verification.notes: Verified source/model/migration absence of active-day uniqueness and handler transaction; dual SQL commit is predicted, not executed.

findings.origin: Coordinator targeted semantic comparison SEM-MIRROR-027; independent challenge by financial_integrity_continuation.

source_record.status: SOURCE_SUPPORTED_CONCURRENT_ACTIVE_DAY_RISK; NO ACTIVE-DAY UNIQUE CONSTRAINT OR HANDLER TRANSACTION FOUND

implementation_readiness.source_confirmed_behavior: BusinessDayRules.Open rejects any existing active day (Open, Closing, Reopened), and OpenBusinessDayHandler queries those statuses before insertion. Two distinct RequestIds can race: both may read an empty active set, both pass the domain rule, and both insert because the current FalahDbContext BusinessDayEntity model and the initial BusinessDays migration show only unique OpenRequestId, while OpenShiftHandler explicitly has a filtered unique Shift.Status=Open index as the database race-safety net. This is a source-supported concurrency candidate, not a reproduced database race. It is a semantic invariant comparison between analogous lifecycle paths, not a claim of literal duplicated code.
implementation_readiness.root_cause: Active-day admission is a read-check-insert invariant. OpenBusinessDayHandler reads current active rows and invokes BusinessDayRules.Open before a separate insert; there is no shared transaction/conditional state claim, while the schema has uniqueness only by request ID.
implementation_readiness.preconditions: Two authorized open commands with distinct RequestIds begin while no active day is visible; both complete the query/domain check before either inserts. No unreviewed deployment-wide serialization is in effect.
implementation_readiness.impact: More than one active business day may be persisted, making day attribution, financial close blockers/snapshots, and active-day lookups ambiguous. No actual duplicate day or accounting loss has been reproduced.
counterevidence: Same OpenRequestId is protected by unique index and replay handling; candidate specifically uses distinct IDs.
BusinessDayRules correctly blocks a second active row in a sequentially refreshed read.
OpenShift demonstrates the application uses a filtered unique index for an analogous single-active invariant, but that index is Shift-only.
SQL Server provider plus RCSI does not itself establish uniqueness; no row/range/application lock was found in the shown open path.
External reverse proxy, scheduler, service host or database trigger coordination was not certified; source scan is not proof about deployment infrastructure.
implementation_readiness.proposed_fix_or_owner_decision: Confirm the invariant scope. If one active BusinessDay is intended, enforce it at the same persistence boundary as the single-open-shift invariant (provider-appropriate active-row uniqueness or a serialized admission row/lock covering Open and Reopen), and make losing admission return a stable conflict without partial side effects. Preserve same-request idempotency. Do not rely solely on a pre-insert read.
regression_tests: Barrier-controlled concurrent opens with two distinct RequestIds: at most one active day commits; loser receives a conflict and no second row is created.
Same RequestId replay returns the original day without a second row.
Concurrent reopen of one day and open of another cannot create two active days if global invariant is confirmed.
Sequential open while Open, Closing, or Reopened rejects; after valid close, a new day opens.
Run against supported SQL Server provider and two independent DbContext/process instances; assert database-level invariant.
acceptance_criteria: A documented owner policy establishes the active-day scope (global or per defined partition).

If global single-active-day remains intended, every Open/Reopen transition is serialized or constrained by database-enforced uniqueness so concurrent instances cannot persist more than one active day.
A losing concurrency attempt leaves no partial state and the existing same-request replay contract remains intact.
implementation_readiness.runtime_limits: Static source/model/migration comparison only. No application tests, SQL Server/provider behavior, database instance, race schedule, or deployment-level lock was executed.

independent_challenge.disposition: SOURCE_SUPPORTED_CONCURRENT_ACTIVE_DAY_RISK; NO ACTIVE-DAY UNIQUE CONSTRAINT OR HANDLER TRANSACTION FOUND
independent_challenge.confidence: High for configured application source and SQL Server EF model/migration scope. Concurrent dual commit is a predicted outcome, not observed SQL execution; external deployment-level coordination remains unknown.

source_record.title: SafeDrop may attribute a later drawer movement to a closed shift and change its reprinted breakdown
source_record.root_cause: SafeDrop validates only that the request ShiftId exists; it does not require the referenced shift to remain Open. It posts with the current open BusinessDayId plus that request ShiftId. ShiftReconciliation later selects Posted safe_drop rows by ShiftId. Reprinting a close slip recomputes detail from current rows but restores the stored expected, actual and difference headline.
source_record.source_mechanism: If the BusinessDay remains open, a user can submit a SafeDrop referencing a Closed shift. The transaction moves drawer cash to Main and tags the movement with both current day and the requested historical shift. ShiftReconciliation then includes it in the historical shift safe-drop component. ComposeShiftCloseSlipAsync recomputes the breakdown but uses the saved close headline. This supports later component drift on reprint, not cash loss or change to the posted ledger total.
source_record.impact: The closed shift close-slip component breakdown can reflect a later SafeDrop while its headline remains the original saved close values. This can reduce reconciliation clarity or attribute later custody to an earlier shift if that is not the intended policy.
preconditions: A business day is still open.
Caller has safe_drop authorization.
The request references a valid shift row already Closed.
A shift close slip is recomposed after that movement.
counterevidence: SafeDropHandler comments say requiring only an existing shift intentionally preserves reference-application behavior.
A delayed custody transfer may intentionally belong to the earlier shift while the same business day remains open.
The movement remains a drawer-to-main treasury transfer through the common protected-balance and journal transaction; no monetary loss is shown.
Existing integration tests cover SafeDrop direction with an open shift and cashier movement open-shift validation, but not this post-close sequence.
source_record.recommendation: Owner policy decision required. If SafeDrop against closed shifts is disallowed, enforce the chosen shift-status invariant in a way that serializes correctly with CloseShift; a stale pre-transaction status read is insufficient. If late safe drops are allowed, represent their later attribution/revision explicitly and make reprints distinguish immutable close-time totals from subsequent movements. Do not silently mutate the saved close headline.

independent_verification.conclusion: WPF SubmitRefundAsync creates rreq-{Guid.NewGuid()} for each invocation, invokes RefundAsync once, and resets IsRefunding in finally. WPF ApiClient posts and parses HTTP results but has no transport-exception-to-OutcomeUnknown conversion. WinUI builds a request only when _pendingRefund is null; CompleteRefundAsync stores it before send, retains it for OutcomeUnknown, and reuses it on the next submit. It rotates the ID only after success. This is an in-memory recovery context; durability across process restart is not established by these files. A manual WPF re-submit after an ambiguous transport exception is a distinct idempotency command. If a prior partial refund committed, the second command may be another separately recorded refund, subject to the remaining-refund clamp and authorization. This is not evidence of an automatic retry, duplicate posting under one key, over-refund, or cash/account loss. Server locks the order and checks the protected source balance before recording the refund. A full already-refunded order has no positive remainder and is rejected. Disposition: Corroborate the source-described client difference and conditional recovery concern. Keep severity conditional/low; do not classify as duplicate-payment/over-refund or merge with FIN-CAND-REFUND-REPLAY-001. The latter remains a separate server replay-result edge, not evidence of multiple movement postings.

source_record.root_cause: WPF SubmitRefundAsync creates a fresh RefundRequestId per invocation and WPF ApiClient does not expose transport ambiguity as OutcomeUnknown or retain the request for replay. WinUI keeps _pendingRefund and retries the same request ID during the current ViewModel lifetime.
source_record.source_mechanism: The server keys refund replay by refund-{RefundRequestId}; a distinct WPF submit is a distinct command. Server order locking, remaining-refundable clamping and protected source balance constrain results. The source does not show automatic retry or over-refund; the conditional concern is an operator manually submitting another partial refund before reconciling an uncertain first result. WinUI pending state is memory-only.
source_record.impact: If WPF is supported/deployed, response loss after a successful partial refund can leave the operator without explicit unknown-outcome recovery; a subsequent submit generates a new key and may create a separate additional partial refund. Impact depends on deployment, transport outcome and operator action.
preconditions: WPF client is supported/deployed.
A partial refund commits but its response is lost or cannot be parsed.
Operator submits again before authoritative order/refund reconciliation.
Remaining order amount and protected account balance permit another partial refund.
counterevidence: Current active cashier was identified as WinUI; WPF deployment is unknown.
Server clamps refunds to remaining order amount and protects account balance; no over-refund or cash loss is shown.
Same-key server replay is covered by checked-in test source.
WinUI pending retry state is not shown as durable across process restart.
No automatic WPF retry is evidenced.
source_record.recommendation: If WPF is supported, route refund commands through explicit unknown-outcome state and retain/reconcile the same request ID before allowing a new submit. If WPF is retired, record that operational fact. Decide whether WinUI unresolved refund intent must survive restart; if so, persist a safe pending key or require authoritative refund lookup before another command. Preserve server amount and account guards.
required_regression_tests: Inject response loss after server commit in WPF; retry must reuse the key or require server reconciliation before a new command.
WinUI timeout/response loss then retry in same ViewModel must use the same ID and return one receipt.
Restart after unresolved WinUI outcome must follow owner-selected recovery policy.
A deliberate new partial refund with a distinct ID remains allowed when the order/account permit it.
Retain same-key replay and distinct-key cumulative cap integration tests.

implementation_readiness.current_behavior: GetDeliveryOutcomesReportAsync filters all non-settled custody rows without a date filter, counts them, then sums CollectedPiastres into DTO field UnsettledCustodyExpectedPiastres. DeliveryRules.CreateCashCustody initializes Expected to responsibility and Collected to zero; assignment persists both. RecordDeliveryResultHandler populates Collected only when Delivered and stores any variance. OwnerDashboardQueryService independently projects unsettled custody as the sum of ExpectedPiastres. The report UI binds the mismatched DTO amount. Thus an assigned/out-for-delivery order can count as unsettled while its labeled expected amount is zero; a delivered variance can also make collected differ from expected.
implementation_readiness.preconditions: At least one non-prepaid delivery has been assigned (creating Open custody) and has not yet reached Delivered, or a delivered custody has an approved recorded variance. No real runtime state was created or queried.
implementation_readiness.impact: If the DTO/UI contract means expected cash at driver risk, the report underreports that exposure while delivery is in transit and diverges from the owner dashboard. If it intentionally means cash already collected but not settled, the aggregation may be deliberate but DTO name and tests are misleading. No loss, duplicate payment, or ledger corruption is established.
implementation_readiness.proposed_remediation: Confirm report contract. Existing DTO name, owner dashboard, and test comments support ExpectedPiastres: if that is the intended meaning, sum c.ExpectedPiastres. If the intended metric is collected-but-unsettled, rename the DTO/display and retain/add a distinct expected-at-risk metric so the two values are not conflated.
required_regression_tests: Open assigned COD custody before Delivered: report count is one and expected amount equals responsibility; collected amount is zero.
Delivered with exact collection: expected and collected equal and both projections agree.
Delivered with approved shortage/overage: expected remains original responsibility while collected reflects actual; report fields follow chosen names/contract.
After settlement, unsettled count/amount falls to zero; settled-period totals remain date-filtered.
Historical DailyStatement queried before/after a later settlement: assert current-now versus as-of-date policy explicitly.

Assigned, open COD custody before delivery: query the same unsettled cohort through the delivery report and owner dashboard; assert both expected-at-risk amounts equal the original cash responsibility, collected is zero, and counts agree.

Approved variance cross-view case: expected-at-risk remains the original responsibility in both projections while collected reflects the actual driver collection; assert the chosen field names and values explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: DTO field name and source aggregate express the same amount.
Owner dashboard and delivery report agree for the same non-settled custody cohort when they claim to show expected custody.
In-transit and variance cases are covered by tests; no real printer or financial operation is needed.
Historical statement temporal semantics are documented separately.
Before delivery, delivery report and owner dashboard agree on expected cash responsibility for the same open custody cohort while collected remains zero.
counterevidence: The application may intend this field to represent collected-but-unsettled cash; however the DTO explicitly says Expected, the existing integration assertion comments expected responsibility, and the owner dashboard uses ExpectedPiastres.
Existing reporting test checks the row only after full amount is collected, so Expected and Collected are equal in that test.
No API, SQL Server, or UI execution was performed; no current incident is known.

coverage_limit: Registry consolidation is not validation or completed security coverage. Original evidence is preserved losslessly.
